claims.text: The conventional high-entropy-alloy intermediate layer has high mechanical strength but limited heat-transfer efficiency.
The conventional alloy contains randomly oriented nanoprecipitates.
Controlled directional annealing can induce an oriented network of coherent nanoprecipitates.
Directional annealing reorients nanoprecipitates along the dominant heat-flow direction.
Aligned coherent nanoprecipitates act as thermal bridges.
Nanoprecipitate alignment creates effective heat-conduction pathways that enhance thermal conductivity.
Coherent inter-precipitate interfaces are responsible for maintaining the alloy's structural strength.
Directional annealing can preserve the coherent interfaces needed for structural strength while aligning the nanoprecipitates.
Compared with the untreated alloy, the annealed alloy will have significantly higher thermal conductivity.
The annealed alloy will retain robust mechanical properties under high-temperature and high-load conditions.
Temperatures above 500°C and high mechanical loading mimic typical plasma-facing-reactor operating conditions.
Deleterious phase changes or precipitate coarsening would prevent the proposed benefit.
The proposed benefit requires the oriented microstructure to remain stable during continuous high-temperature and high-load exposure.
The magnitude of the heat-transfer improvement is unquantified.
The long-term stability of the oriented nanoprecipitate network under cyclic reactor conditions is unquantified.
